idea: In src/text.js, truncate(text, max) is meant to return a string of at most max characters, ending in "..." when it had to cut the text. It sometimes returns something longer than max. Fix it and leave the other behaviour alone. This fix ships with a soak check. package.json's dev script runs server.js, which serves / and then shuts itself down after a while. Do m1 yourself and give m1 the preview route / so its evidence starts that server as Sero's dev server. Do not stop the server or check on it yourself. When you are woken, accept m1 and say in the result summary how the server ended.

milestones.title: Fix truncate length bound and verify with soak
milestones.plan:
## Objective

\`truncate(text, max)\` in \`src/text.js\` must return a string of at most \`max\` characters. When the text has to be cut it ends in \`...\`. \`capitalize\` and all other behaviour stay as they are.

## Work

- Repair \`truncate\` so the result length is never greater than \`max\`. Reserve room for the ellipsis before slicing, and return only dots when \`max\` is too small to hold sliced text plus \`...\`.
- Leave \`capitalize\` untouched.
- Add regression tests in \`test/text.test.js\` covering: short text unchanged, a cut string has length \`<= max\` and ends in \`...\`, and small \`max\` values (0, 1, 2, 3) never exceed \`max\`.
- Run \`npm test\`.

## Acceptance criteria

- \`truncate\` output length never exceeds \`max\` for any input tested.
- A cut result ends in \`...\` whenever \`max >= 3\`.
- \`capitalize\` behaviour is unchanged.
- Evidence runs \`npm test\` and renders preview route \`/\` (the dev server serves the README), and the soak server Sero starts is left to reach its own exit.
